title: "Distributed Configuration"
description: "A complete unit in the microservices architecture learning path."

## Why this unit matters

Separate operational settings from service binaries. Study Config Server, distributed refresh via Bus, and managed configuration releases with Apollo.

The same shop remains the anchor: Product owns catalogue information, User owns customer information, and Order coordinates checkout. Read each chapter in order to see which new requirement motivates the next design decision.

## Lessons

1. **[Configuration Management Principles](config-principles.qmd)**
2. **[Spring Cloud Config](spring-cloud-config.qmd)**
3. **[Spring Cloud Bus and Refresh](spring-cloud-bus.qmd)**
4. **[Apollo Configuration Centre](apollo-config.qmd)**

## Learning objective

After this unit, describe the dependency or operational problem **before** naming a framework; draw the relevant call/event path; state the failure mode and trade-off; and explain how the concept applies to a small TypeScript or NestJS service.

## Source mapping and example

**Supplied source:** Day 4 §2–3. The content is an original explanation of the supplied course's topics and not a reproduction of its Java code. Start the [single-file Node.js shop lab](../examples/README.md) to inspect the related HTTP endpoints. Framework-specific components that are not present in the lab are explained as architectural patterns.
